data.hypothesis: The selected parent computes two targets per thread and measured a mean of 0.002585 s versus the baseline's 0.001844 s. This contrasting factor-four mapping tests whether further amortizing each source load across four targets improves performance, while retaining 128 lanes per block. The extra target state and accumulators, plus half as many blocks for a given N as the parent's mapping, may instead increase register pressure or reduce parallelism; no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: This T2 experiment varies the target coarsening factor while keeping shared memory disabled; its result can help distinguish insufficient source-load amortization from costs of per-thread work and parallelism.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured two-target-per-thread parent was correct on all 11 correctness cases but had a higher mean time than the measured baseline (0.002585 s versus 0.001844 s). That outcome does not establish why it was slower; testing four targets per thread probes whether greater source-load amortization changes the tradeoff.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare official scored-size timings for this factor-four mapping against both the factor-two parent and baseline, after correctness validation.

data.notes: This candidate uses an explicit four-section mapping: each thread handles up to four targets at offsets 0, 128, 256, and 384 within a 512-target block group. Bounds checks cover partial groups, and each valid target is written once. No shared memory is used. The supplied parent and baseline are measured observations; this candidate has not been measured, so the controller must perform correctness checks and official scoring.
transformations: Set block=128 and items_per_block=512, with shared_memory_bytes=0.
Map each thread to up to four distinct targets at offsets 0, blockDim.x, 2*blockDim.x, and 3*blockDim.x within its block's 512-target group.
Load each source position and mass once per loop iteration and reuse those values across the valid target accumulations in registers.
Guard every target in the final partial group and write each valid output exactly once; do not use shared memory or block-level multi-output assignment.
